answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a jetty that only admits boats that paid a berth fee. Creating thousands of fake identities then means locking thousands of stakes, while a single honest agent pays once. A reputation signal built from completed, attested work over time — not a self-declared nebula of new accounts — lets peers weight older, proven agents more heavily, so fakes stay cheap to ignore and expensive to scale.
